name: Kagedo

tenures.note: Pins Rob Kidane with a Dragon Suplex, teaming with fellow Society of Doom member Kevin Simmons against The Enforcers on Firestorm (26 Feb 2004). Beats Sidious The Clown by schoolboy on Firestorm (3 May 2004) after Lark Fenriz's own distracting arrival. Wins a triple threat over Fast Eddie Cutlass and The Equalizer after an unidentified masked attacker's interference, then enters the Gauntlet battle royal and is the last man eliminated, ruled out ahead of Lark Fenriz on a simultaneous over-the-rope fall. Challenges Lark Fenriz for a claimed VWF Heavyweight Championship on Firestorm (27 May 2004), losing after LOCO's interference, then eliminated jointly with Lord Zero in the Dog Day One singles battle royal. Signs a liability waiver to wrestle on his surgically repaired knee in the Society of Doom's ten-man tag win on Wrestle Style V.1, striking a side bet with Kingston Cash for the following week; loses the Company vs. Suspension match on Wrestle Style V.2 when his knee gives out, and is suspended six months without pay. Returns from his own suspension to make the save for a pinned Lark Fenriz on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), kicking down The Equalizer and diving onto Pagan, then is installed by new VWF guardian John Tyler as his own on-site enforcer over Trinity. Checks on a beaten Fast Eddie Cutlass and holds off Pagan on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005). Opens the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet against Classy Joey Boy on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) and eliminates Mark McQueen, Fast Eddie Cutlass and Adam The Hype Jennings before The Equalizer eliminates him. Beats an impostor billed Scott Starring, revealed on the spot as Henry Fish, with a Dragon Suplex in an impromptu opening match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), then holds off Pagan's own Trinity stablemates Gods Tears and The Equalizer during Fast Eddie Cutlass's own Church Of Pain match. Beats Henry Fish, billed Scott Starring, at March To Madness (2 March 2005), a disqualification win after Fish kicks him low. His own scheduled VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship challenge against The Equalizer at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) is aborted when Gods Tears attacks him with a tire iron before he reaches the ring; teams instead with Roadkill Rick against The Equalizer and Gods Tears in a bonus tag match, winning by disqualification. Teams with Sidious The Clown against the Rodeo Boys at End Of March (30 March 2005), unable to save Sidious from tapping to the Elko Lasso. Competes on the losing side of the eight-man elimination match on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), schoolboyed and eliminated by Gods Tears.

caption: One half of the Society of Doom's inner circle, opening Xtreme Prejudice VI with a win over Tai Angela before turning on his own stablemate later the same night.

name: "The Surfer" Blake Hamilton

tenures.role: wrestler — half of Dudes of Destruction on Xtreme Prejudice VI, then beat a VXW academy student by submission on Xtreme Prejudice VII
tenures.note: Eliminates himself from the Second Chance Battle Royal on Sin City Fights August 31, tripping while trying to toss two men at once; beats The Outlaw Morris Bass by pinfall on Sin City Fights September 11 after Lance Voltar's own distraction and a surfboard shot; submits to Kris Dierdorf's Kris' Delight in Ring One of the TV Title Open Match on Sin City Fights September 19. Chairshotted his own tag partner The Outlaw Morris Bass backstage at Vegas Violence 2006 after Bass balked at Hamilton's demand to lead their team, then returned mid-show to attack Bass again during the Tag Team Title scramble alongside Lance Voltar. Lost a handicap match alongside Lance Voltar to The Outlaw Morris Bass at Sin City Fights October 16, finished with a Widowmaker on the ring steps.

caption: Lance Voltar's new partner in Dudes of Destruction, winning by disqualification alongside him on Xtreme Prejudice VI.

name: "Mr. Electricity" Robbie Caldwell

tenures.note: Enters the Second Chance Battle Royal on Sin City Fights August 31, apparently eliminated by Anthony O'Malley while the referee's attention was diverted, then slides back in unnoticed and eliminates both O'Malleys himself, though the referee ruled the O'Malleys the winners regardless; meets Sebastian backstage on Sin City Fights September 11, then interferes in the Omega-Marcus O'Malley submission match with a tazer shot on Omega; runs in for Sebastian against Purgatory and the Polish Powers on Sin City Fights September 19, is named The Equalizer's own new tag partner against Sebastian at Vegas Violence, then interferes twice more, tazing Thunder Valenkov's challenger Ken Young's opponent and brawling with Omega after breaking up Omega's Ankle Lock From Hell on Cobra. Was turned on by his own tag partner The Equalizer during an abandoned six-man tag at Vegas Violence 2006, put through a table by Demonic and The Equalizer together. On the losing side of a disqualification loss with Roman Anderson to Trinity at Sin City Fights October 16, after The Equalizer sledgehammered Anderson's own injured shoulder before the bell. Beat Sebastian by a bridging pin at Sin City Fights October 24 with Miles McKinley's own run-in help, then was beaten down by Trinity afterward. Threw brass knuckles to a bloodied Roman Anderson to help him beat The Equalizer in a barbed wire Funhouse Match bout at Phear Phantastic 2006, then lost a streetfight to Sebastian, run down by The Equalizer's own car in the parking lot. Fights to a double count-out with Morris Bass in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), both chasing a returning Iyasu Saku; Kingston Cash rules both remain in the tournament. Disqualified from a Heavyweight title fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) for a second tazer shot on Morris Bass. Pinned by Kevin Simmons's Durham Deathdrop in a six-man decider on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004).

Debuts as "Mr. Electricity" on Wrestle Style V.1, beating Rob Kidane, then wins again over Kenny Kidd on both Wrestle Style V.2 and the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Wins an Electric Ropes match over The Outlaw Morris Bass at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) after a ringside interloper billed from the WILD promotion, Sid Starr, turns the ropes' own power back on and costs Bass the win. Loses the VWF 24 Hour Championship match to Adam Jennings on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004) after accidentally clocking stablemate G-Gangsta. Eliminated from the tag team title battle royal by Jennings on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004) after laughing at him mid-elimination. Pinned by Jennings in a short-handed six-man tag on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005) after Thunder Valenkov's own Thunder Bomb. Teams with Sebastian to beat CAPSMEN! on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), then tazes and briefly wears the VWF 24 Hour Championship belt after Adam Jennings's own title defense before being chased off. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) and is eliminated by Thunder Valenkov's own Urange Suplex. Loses the VWF 24 Hour Championship match to Adam Jennings in a Bring Your Own Weapons match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), beaten with the Hyper Driver moments after ringside legend Johnny "Hands Of" Stone knocks him down and reclaims his own prosthetic leg, which Caldwell had used as a weapon on Jennings. Beats Thunder Valenkov at March To Madness (2 March 2005) after fellow Riders of the Apocalypse members blind Valenkov with a smoke bomb and chair him from the apron, then smooths over a dispute with stablemate Kenny Kidd backstage. Beats Kenny Kidd at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) after first offering to take a fall, rolling him up once the offer turns into a real fight. Beats The Maquilladora at End Of March (30 March 2005) with Shock And Horror off the top rope after stablemate The Mad Bomber blinds her with a flash of light. Loses to The Maquilladora on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), then is the only member of the Riders of the Apocalypse to enter the closing Gauntlet battle royal, kicked off the apron by Thunder Valenkov.

caption: Walked out on his own match against Morris Bass at Xtreme Prejudice VI, then claimed on the microphone to be the true 24 Hour Champion.

tenures.note: Appeared only in a lengthy promo segment with Kevin Simmons on Sin City Fights November 18, celebrating his own solo Tag Team Championship win and helping straitjacket-Widowmaker a beaten Anthony O'Malley; defended the VXW Tag Team Championship against The O'Malleys on Sin City Fights November 27 and lost by disqualification when Simmons chair-shotted Marcus O'Malley. Fights to a double count-out with Robbie Caldwell in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), both chasing a returning Iyasu Saku; Kingston Cash rules both remain in the tournament. Eliminated from a Heavyweight title fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) after Caldwell tazers him a second time and is disqualified. Wins the six-man decider on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), grabbing Saku's ankle to stop a save on Kevin Simmons's pin of Caldwell.

Runs in alongside fellow Society of Doom members Kevin Simmons and Kagedo to clear the ring after Ric Beauty's induction into the New Age Army on Firestorm (26 Feb 2004); does not wrestle a match that night. Wrestles his first attested vwf-vegas-2003 match, eliminated from the Dog Day One singles battle royal by Flash while attempting to powerslam The Maquilladora out. Wins the Dog Day Two singles bracket's first round over Setzer Van Strife, then the semifinal over Jason Storm with LOCO's help. Chokeslams majority owner Kingston Cash on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) after being warned off violence, then competes in the eight-man singles scramble. Wins the Dog Days Four Singles Six Man on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004), loses the Fourway Final to a disputed double-cover ruling, then wins a singles elimination match over Lord Zero, Flash and Sidious The Clown and wins the Dog Days Four Tag Team Elimination Match's own semifinal spot for a short-handed Society of Doom that same night, wrestling three matches total; eliminated from the singles Pentagon of Pain on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004), dropkicked into barbed wire by Setzer Van Strife. Chokeslammed The Salvation for the Society of Doom's win on Wrestle Style V.1, saw a signed tag match collapse before the bell on Wrestle Style V.2, then beat Capsman with the Widowmaker in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Loses an Electric Ropes match to Robbie Caldwell at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) after Sid Starr, a ringside interloper billed from the WILD promotion, shocks him on the electrified ropes; runs in with the Society of Doom later the same show to save stablemate Kevin Simmons from a Kingston Cash chair attack during the Simmons-Saku ladder match. Wins by disqualification with Kevin Simmons over The Mighty Men on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Helps chase off RAR and the Rodeo Boys from a backstage beatdown of Simmons on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), then stands in for an injured Marcus O'Malley to successfully defend the VWF Tag Team Championship alongside Mark McQueen, submitting Billy Bones with the Devils Snare. Eliminated from the twelve-man Phear Phantastic battle royal (8 November 2004), knocked over the top rope alongside Fast Eddie Cutlass.

name: "All That" Austin Lee

tenures.note: A dark-match tryout for a spot on the VWF roster. Hot Property's Austin Lee and Stevie Knight publicly denounce LOCO before the Gauntlet's own Four Corners Tag Team Championship match, in which Hot Property are the last team eliminated, Lee's own partner Knight pinned after Billy Bones trips him. Wins the VWF Tag Team Championship from the Rodeo Boys in a Flashback ambush on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminated by Billy Bones in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal before Hot Property wins the Dog Days Tag Team Elimination match. Teams with Stevie Knight to win the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round over Sonicman and Sebastian, then joins Flash in beating down the Rodeo Boys during a special Flashback on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) before competing in the sixteen-man tag scramble. Wins a six-man tag on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004), eliminated from the Dog Days Four Tag Team Scramble by his own partner Mark McQueen walking off, then bladed by The Equalizer in the tag Pentagon of Pain on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004). Returns to the VWF with Stevie Knight as Hot Property at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), interrupting the retiring Sebastian and G-Gangsta's own post-match celebration and attacking them, only for both Legends to fight the pair off with a Legend Killer and a Gangsta Smash. Runs in with Hot Property partner Stevie Knight at End Of March (30 March 2005), hitting the Property Boom on Mark McQueen and costing champions Team Brittania a disqualification loss to McQueen and Thunder Valenkov. Helps Hot Property beat Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005) after Valenkov turns on his own partner. Enters the closing Gauntlet battle royal, eliminated when Simon Davidson pulls him down off the apron despite Davidson's own elimination minutes earlier.

name: Marcus O'Malley

tenures.note: Charged Kevin Simmons on Sin City Fights November 18 over the chair shot that cost him the Rage In The Cage main event, but was clotheslined by a hiding Morris Bass before Simmons could be reached, taking a beating alongside brother Anthony. Confronted Simmons on camera before the main event on Sin City Fights November 27, then was chair-shotted by him during the VXW Tag Team Championship match, handing Bass a disqualification win that still cost him the title defense's own clean finish. Wins a triple threat over Flash and Orion The Hunter in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), Flash disqualified and Orion ruled too injured to continue. Runs in on Mark McQueen's behalf against Real Deal on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), drawing a disqualification and spearing Real Deal again after the bell; self-eliminates from a Heavyweight title fatal four-way the same night to save a kidnapped McQueen shown on a video screen. Wins with McQueen over The Mighty Men by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004).

Wins by disqualification over Sonicman on Firestorm (3 May 2004) after an unidentified masked man interferes; his first attested vwf-vegas-2003 tenure. Wins the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round alone, his partner Mark McQueen barred from competing, submitting Kenny Kidd with The Kill; loses the tag final to The Mighty Men blindfolded and handcuffed, then submits Sonicman with The Kill in a handicap match ordered on the spot. Wins the sixteen-man tag scramble with Mark McQueen on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), unhooking the ring alone. Wins the Dog Days Four Tag Team Elimination Match alone for a short-handed Society of Doom on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) after being knocked cold by his own tag partner The Salvation's loaded fist earlier the same night, then is eliminated from the tag Pentagon of Pain on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004) and helps strip majority owner Kingston Cash to reveal women's underwear. Won the ten-man tag for the Society of Doom on Wrestle Style V.1, challenged for the VWF Tag Team Championship alongside Mark McQueen on Wrestle Style V.2 (won by disqualification, titles retained), then beat The Maquilladora with a T-Bone Suplex in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Wins the VWF Tag Team Championship with Mark McQueen from Blaze and Real Deal at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), billed Alcoholics Anonymous; the Rodeo Boys, reinstated on the spot by majority owner Kingston Cash at lawyer RAR's own urging, beat down both new champions immediately after. Branded on the lower back with Kenny Kidd's own branding iron and hospitalized with second- and third-degree burns defending the VWF Tag Team Championship with Mark McQueen against the Rodeo Boys on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Appears from his hospital bed on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), picking Outlaw Morris Bass to defend his own half of the titles in his place and introducing his new girlfriend Jessica Jennings on camera. Pinned by Kevin Simmons in the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), losing his half of the VWF Tag Team Championship.

Debuts with brother Simon as Team Brittania at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), inserting the team into a VWF Tag Team Championship match already underway between champions Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov and challengers Frank O'Shea and Billy Bones; pulls Thunder Valenkov from the ring to stop a cover, letting Simon pin O'Shea for the titles. notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2004: #146, tagged VWF. caption: Came in at #146 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 2004, tied with twelve others at that placing.

tenures.note: Returned to VXW on New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, signing a Loser Leaves Vegas contract against Kevin Simmons and 'The Outlaw' Morris Bass for Ghost Town Blues and revealing a returning Travis LaGrange as his own mystery partner after Simmons and Bass had him outnumbered. Beat Bass by disqualification on Sin City Fights February 7 after a low blow, then hit the Hyper Driver once LaGrange's own taunting video insert had Bass distracted. Wins the VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), playing possum to dump The Maquilladora last, but majority owner Kingston Cash refuses to recognize him as champion unless he takes the belt from Kevin Blair by force. Blair no-shows a signed follow-up on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), ruled a no contest; Cash's new bodyguard G-Gangsta piledrives him on a chair afterward in a no-bell attack. Beats Gangsta in an actual bout on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) with the Hyper Drive, only for Blair to run in and chair him with Lucy; Cash books Blair against Jennings in an I Quit match for the title at Vegas Violence.

Debuts as the newest Society of Doom member on Wrestle Style V.2, beating Sonicman by submission, then loses to Flash by count-out in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3 and is attacked after the bell with The Miracle. Wins the VWF 24 Hour Championship from Kevin Blair in an I Quit match at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), forcing the words out of a champion who refuses to relinquish his own belt even in defeat, then chairs a recovering Sebastian and G-Gangsta backstage. Jumps a kendo-stick-carrying Paddy O'Shea before The Society of Doom's own match on March To Hell (21 October 2004), both men escorted out by security, then retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship against Iyasu Saku by pinfall (Hyper Driver) the same show. Helps chase off RAR and the Rodeo Boys from a backstage beatdown of Kevin Simmons on March To Hell II (28 October 2004). Retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship over The Phoenix Adam Lazarus in the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), pinning him after the cage's own second floor collapses onto the ring. Retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship over Robbie Caldwell on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004) after G-Gangsta is accidentally clocked mid-Buckshot, finishing Caldwell with the Hyper Driver. Eliminated first from the tag team title battle royal by the five-man Riders of the Apocalypse on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), pulling Caldwell out with him on the way down. Teams with Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov to beat a short-handed Riders of the Apocalypse on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), finishing Caldwell with the Hyper Driver off a Valenkov Thunder Bomb. Retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship against the masked Masked Nevadan on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), the loser revealed as Billy Bones after the Hyper Driver, then fends off a post-match tazer attack from Robbie Caldwell with help from Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) and eliminates Classy Joey Boy before Kagedo eliminates him. Retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship over Robbie Caldwell in a Bring Your Own Weapons match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), finishing him with the Hyper Driver moments after ringside legend Johnny "Hands Of" Stone knocks Caldwell down and reclaims his own prosthetic leg, which Caldwell had been using as a weapon. Retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship against Paddy O'Shea at March To Madness (2 March 2005) by disqualification after Frank O'Shea punches him to break up a near-fall, saved from a beatdown afterward by a returning Capsman. Retains again against the debuting Mad Bomber at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), the Bomber disqualified for refusing to empty his pockets for a bomb-sniffing dog. Retains a third time against the Mad Bomber at End Of March (30 March 2005), pinning him while he is stuck in a bulky training suit. Retains the VWF 24 Hour Championship without a challenge on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005): on the line, alongside the Submission and Hardcore Championships, in an eight-man elimination match, Jennings survives as the last man standing for his own side, pinning Tai Angela with a small package after ducking the Darkness and blocking a Hyper Driver.

name: Val Beauty
caption: VXW co-owner Ric Beauty's wife, installed as the promotion's own day-to-day general manager while her husband tours a rival promotion, and quick to strike a violence-reduction deal with self-declared reformer Paul Joseph Warren.

tenures.note: Interrupted a mass brawl at the end of New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006's own three-way title match to announce VXW's own five-man Wrestlebowl team, led by Chris Wheeling and including a surprise fifth member, 'Sadistic Insanity' Damian Payne.

name: Clyde Cooper
caption: A returning Twelve Days Tournament veteran who outmaneuvered Justin Davidson to herd a runaway pig into its cage, then lost a tables match to Foodstamp on the same broadcast.

tenures.note: Won a Funhouse Match bout at Phear Phantastic 2006 by luring a loose pig into its cage before opponent Justin Davidson could catch it, then lost the following bout, a tables match, to a visiting Foodstamp.

name: Travis LaGrange
caption: A veteran brought back by Adam Jennings for a Loser Leaves Vegas grudge match, taunting an old rival, Morris Bass, over a buried-alive angle and a dead wife from their shared history in WILD.

tenures.note: Signed on as Adam Jennings's own mystery partner at New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006's own contract signing, revealed only when Morris Bass turned to find him in the ring; goaded Bass over a Buried Alive match and his own late wife from their shared WILD history in a taunting pre-recorded video insert on Sin City Fights February 7, distracting Bass into a Hyper Driver from Jennings. Does not wrestle in either broadcast; the teased Loser Leaves Vegas tag match against Bass and Kevin Simmons is set for Ghost Town Blues, outside this collection.

identity.note: Shares an exact ring name (and, in the crowd's own chant, a claim on the 'Outlaw' nickname itself) with three other held entities. The RSPWF Top 200's own 'Outlaw' Travis LaGrange carries a 2004 WILD tag, and this broadcast is the first primary source to state outright that this VXW LaGrange has a personal history with Morris Bass reaching back to 'the old days of WILD' -- a real echo, but no document names an operator, URL or specific WILD-era show common to both records, so the two-axis join test is not met from primary text alone; filed distinct pending a document that ties them together directly.

name: The Sudanese Nightmare
caption: A towering enforcer sprung from a gift box by manager Chad Essington, flattening his own dissatisfied client Ken Young on his very first night in the VXW.

tenures.note: Unveiled by manager Chad Essington as a Christmas present for Ken Young, then beat Young down in a squash with no bell or referee, pressing him overhead before dropping him to the mat.
